dialogue.content: いろいろとご迷惑をおかけしてしまいすみませんでした。頑張りますのでよろしくお願いいたします。お時間になりましたら、お声かけさせていただきます。
dialogue.English: I apologize for any inconvenience this may have caused. I will do my best, and I appreciate your understanding. I will let you know when it is time.

dialogue.content: いえいえ、大丈夫です！もう少しですね。こちらこそよろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: No, no, it's quite alright! We're almost there. I'm looking forward to it as well.

dialogue.content: こんばんは。相談員です。最初に年齢と性別を教えてください。
dialogue.English: Good evening. I'm the counselor. To begin, could you please tell me your age and gender?

dialogue.content: こんばんは。45歳女です。よろしくお願いします。
dialogue.English: Good evening. I'm a 45-year-old woman. Thank you for having me.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: 本日はどのようなご相談ですか。
dialogue.English: What would you like to talk about today?

dialogue.content: はい、生きることについてです。
dialogue.English: Yes, it's about... life itself.

dialogue.content: なかなか深い感じですね。もう少し具体的に教えてもらってもいいですか。一番話したいことでもだいじょうぶですよ。
dialogue.English: That sounds like a very profound topic. Could you tell me a little more specifically? It's perfectly fine to start with whatever you'd most like to talk about.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。私の実の父が３年前に亡くなりまして。それから、生きることについて私自身疑問というか、執着がなくなった感じがしてしまって。
dialogue.English: Thank you. My biological father passed away three years ago. Since then, I’ve found myself questioning life—or rather, it feels as if I’ve lost my attachment to living.

dialogue.content: それはおつらいことですね。お父様のこと、いきることに対しての疑問、執着、何でもいいので、思ったことをもう少しお聞かせください。
dialogue.English: That must be very difficult for you. Please tell me more about your father, your doubts about living, or your lack of attachment—anything that comes to mind is fine.

dialogue.content: 父の存在がやはり私の中で大きかったのでしょうか。また、結局頑張って生きてもこんな感じで命が終わるんだな、と思うと空しさを感じてしまうんです。
dialogue.English: I suppose my father’s presence was very significant in my life. And when I think that, in the end, life ends like this no matter how hard you try, it gives me a sense of emptiness.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。お父様の存在が大きかったのですね。どのように大きかったのですか。お聞かせいただけたら嬉しいです。
dialogue.English: I see. So your father was a very significant presence in your life. In what way was he significant? I'd appreciate it if you could tell me more.

dialogue.content: はい、父は子どもには優しくてたくさん遊んでくれて、大好きだったんです。ただ、母にはいわゆる亭主関白的でいえのことはほとんどやらず、母とはいろいろあり、熟年離婚をしました。
dialogue.English: Yes, my father was very kind to his children and played with us a lot; I loved him dearly. However, toward my mother, he was what you might call a traditional, domineering husband and did almost nothing around the house. They had their share of problems and ended up divorcing later in life.

dialogue.content: 一時期父にたいして怒りの気持ちがありましたが、やはり時間共に感謝の気持ちと大好きな気持ちは変わらなかったのです。
dialogue.English: For a while, I felt angry with him, but over time, my feelings of gratitude and love for him never really changed.

dialogue.content: そうなのですね。そのようなことで大きな存在と考えてらっしゃるのですね。両親に対してとても誠実に考えたり振り返ったりできることは、とても尊敬です。
dialogue.English: I see. So that's why you see him as such a significant figure. It's truly admirable how sincerely you're able to think about and reflect on your parents.

dialogue.content: ありがとうございます。
dialogue.English: Thank you.

dialogue.content: 虚しさ等は、どの部分で感じるのでしょうか。
dialogue.English: Where, specifically, do you feel this sense of emptiness?

dialogue.content: 生きることへの執着のなさなどもそうですね
dialogue.English: And this lack of attachment to life as well, I suppose.

dialogue.content: やはり、結局頑張って生きても、命はかぎられている。今の健康はどんどん失われ、この先好転していく感じがしないのです。
dialogue.English: After all, no matter how hard you try to live, life is finite. My current health is gradually declining, and I don't feel like things are going to improve from here on out.

dialogue.content: ムックさんの健康があまりよくない感じなのでしょうか。お話しできる範囲でだいじょうぶですよ
dialogue.English: It sounds like your health may not be in a good state, Mukku-san. You only have to share what you're comfortable with.

dialogue.content: そうですね。もともと歯が悪く年々歯を失い、また、よく噛めない、すると食べ物の美味しさが感じにくい。なんだか食べることと生きる気力が結構つながったらいるんだな、とかんじてます。まだ、ありますが。
dialogue.English: Yes. I’ve always had poor teeth and I’ve been losing more year by year. I can’t chew well, so it’s hard to enjoy the taste of food. I'm starting to feel that eating and the will to live are quite connected. There’s more, but…

dialogue.content: 年々いろいろなところが新たにいたくなる、老化ですね。
dialogue.English: Every year, new parts of my body start to ache. It's just aging, I suppose.

dialogue.content: そうですか。それはおつらいですね。でも、そのような中でも、何か楽しみのようなものはありますか。
dialogue.English: I see. That must be difficult. But even with all that, is there anything that brings you joy?

dialogue.content: そうですね。まずは、一応がいて、子ども二人(小学校)は、一応健康に育っていることでしょうか。その、成長ですかね。
dialogue.English: Well, for one, I have a spouse, and my two children, who are in elementary school, are at least growing up healthy. Their growth, I suppose.

dialogue.content: 素晴らしいですね。でも一つ、ぜひお伝えしたいことがあります。それは、健康に育っている部分もあるのではないかと思いますが、ムックさんが健康に育てていらっしゃるということです。ムックさんの努力がそこにあると私は強く思います。
dialogue.English: That's wonderful. But there's one thing I really want to point out. While they are indeed growing up healthy, it is also because you, Mukku-san, are the one raising them to be healthy. I strongly feel that your efforts are a huge part of that.

dialogue.content: その上でこれから、お子さんの成長を見守っていきたいとお考えですか。
dialogue.English: With that in mind, do you want to continue watching over your children's growth from here on?

dialogue.content: そういっていただけると嬉しいです。成長は、楽しみですが、やはり、結局は順番で、今度は私が父の後をおい、30年後くらいに終わるんだな、と思ってしまうんです。
dialogue.English: It makes me happy to hear you say that. I do look forward to their growth, but I can't help but think that, in the end, it's just a matter of taking turns. Now it's my turn to follow in my father's footsteps, and it will all be over for me in about 30 years.

dialogue.content: そうですね。確かに順番はあるかもしれません。私もそうです。でも順番が違っても絶対に嫌だと思います。　お子さんはお母さんに長生きしてもらいたいと考えていると思うのですがいかがでしょうか。
dialogue.English: That's true. There may indeed be a natural order to things. It's the same for me. But I think we would find it absolutely unbearable if that order were broken. I believe your children want their mother to live a long life—how does that feel to you?

dialogue.content: そうですね。子どもにはもちろんそういう気持ちがあると分かります。頭で分かっていて、なぜか気持ちがついていかない、という感じなんです。
dialogue.English: Yes, that's true. I know that my children feel that way, of course. It's like I understand it in my head, but for some reason, my heart just can't catch up.

dialogue.content: そうですよね。そのようなときは、あると思います。　では、頭で考えずとにかく子どものため、大切な人のために全力で活動するのはいかがですか。
dialogue.English: That's right. I think there are certainly times like that. In that case, how about not overthinking it and just giving your all for your children and the people who are important to you?

dialogue.content: 今も一応頑張っているとは思うのですが、時々やっぱり空しさを感じてしまうのです。
dialogue.English: I think I am already trying my best, but sometimes I still just feel this sense of emptiness.

dialogue.content: 頑張る体力も年で落ちてきているみたいで。
dialogue.English: It also feels like my stamina to keep trying is declining with age.

dialogue.content: では、頑張らずに、今の気持ちをあるがままに受け止め許し、虚しさを感じつつも、一日また一日と生きている自分を認め、重ねていくのは、いかがですか。答えは良い意味で先送りで。
dialogue.English: Then, instead of forcing yourself to try, how about this: accept and forgive your current feelings as they are. Acknowledge yourself for living day by day, even while feeling this emptiness, and just let the days build on one another. As for finding an answer, it's okay to postpone it for now, in a good way.

dialogue.content: そうですね。先送り。今は今のままでみとめる…。
dialogue.English: I see... Postponing it. And accepting things as they are for now...

dialogue.content: とりあえず、やってみようかと思います。
dialogue.English: For now, I think I'll give that a try.

dialogue.content: すばらしいですね。お子さんは育っていくのであれば、きっとムックさんは十分に頑張っておられると思います。それ以上がんばる必要はないと思います。今は、お母様、お父様のことの思い出をしっかりと受け止めてもよいのかもしれません。体の不調は、病院にいくことで上向きになるかもしれません。今の一日の中できたこと、よかったことを書ける時に記しておくこともよいのかもしれません。とりあえずやってみることができる方は、自分で自分の未来の扉を開ける方です。応援してます。
dialogue.English: That's wonderful. The fact that your children are growing well is proof that you are already trying more than enough. I don't think you need to push yourself any harder. For now, perhaps it's a good time to fully embrace the memories of your mother and father. Your physical health might improve with a visit to the doctor. It might also be helpful to jot down things you accomplished or things that went well each day, whenever you feel up to it. Someone who can say, 'I'll give that a try,' is someone who can open the door to their own future. I'm rooting for you.

dialogue.content: たくさん応援してくださりありがとうございました。まだしばらく、見つかりそうにないですが、生きることについて自分なりの意味を見つけて行きたいと思います。
dialogue.English: Thank you so much for all your encouragement. I don't think I'll find the answer anytime soon, but I want to try to find my own meaning in living.

dialogue.content: ご自分のご両親の大好きだった部分にヒントがあるかもしれないと感じました。自分の受けたもの、もらったものを人は違えど、どう渡していくかという考え方がよいかもしれませんね。本日は私自身も学びになりました。では、これで終了させていただきます。ありがとうございました。失礼いたします。
dialogue.English: I have a feeling there might be a hint in the aspects of your parents that you loved so dearly. It might be helpful to think about how you can pass on the things you've received from them to others, even if in a different way. Today has been a learning experience for me as well. With that, we'll conclude our session. Thank you very much. Please take care.

dialogue.content: こちらこそありがとうございました。新しい視点をいただきました。
dialogue.English: Thank you as well. You’ve given me a new perspective.
